rules:
Fourth-backbone replication on a single A100-40GB, run under the round-2 protocol, in this order:
  1. pixtral_12b  mistral-community/pixtral-12b (served as mistral-experimental/pixtral-12b, the same
                  repository after a rename), revision c2756cbbb9422eba9f6c5c439a214b0392dfc998.
                  Pixtral-ViT vision encoder + Mistral-NeMo-12B language model. PRIMARY.
  2. idefics3_8b  HuggingFaceM4/Idefics3-8B-Llama3, revision fddb4ff79181e55a994674777e06cd5456ce3dc3.
                  SigLIP vision encoder + Llama-3.1-8B language model.
  3. gemma3_12b   google/gemma-3-12b-it, revision 96b6f1eccf38110c56df3a15bffe176da04bfd80.
                  SigLIP + Gemma-3. CONDITIONAL ARM: the model is gated and access has been requested
                  but not yet granted. It runs if and only if the HF token has access when the A100 job
                  reaches it (or when the job is rerun later); otherwise it is recorded as "not run"
                  (results/courtdyn/backbone4_a100/gemma3_12b/NOT_RUN.json) and nothing is substituted.
Why these backbones: every backbone that has read motion so far is Qwen-derived (Qwen3.5-4B;
Qwen2.5-VL-3B; InternVL3-2B, whose language model is initialised from Qwen2.5). All three here are
non-Qwen in both the vision encoder and the language model. Pixtral-12B is the primary test.
Idefics3-8B shares the Idefics3 architecture (and the frozen SmolVLM2 image policy) with SmolVLM2-2.2B,
which was degenerate at the 4-epoch cap locally; the pair therefore separates scale from architecture:
if Idefics3-8B reads motion under the same recipe, SmolVLM2's failure is a scale boundary, not an
architecture failure; if it does not, the architecture (or its image policy) is implicated. InternVL3-8B
is not trained here; it stays only in the zero-shot sweep (f). Chosen before any training or evaluation
of these models on CourtDyn inputs; these models do not fit the local 8 GB card.

PROTOCOL. The round-2 protocol (results/courtdyn/backbone2_r2/PREREGISTRATION.json, rules_sha256
003f2e1a80e4153cced6a2b512c1aee3bb9fd936ceea821ab8dcea07d3b1c7a4) applies verbatim, with backbone2_r2
read as backbone4_a100/<key>, and with the base-cell clause of the third-backbone record
(results/courtdyn/backbone3_internvl/PREREGISTRATION.json, rules_sha256
8408a84bd433285e8c623957fd268fb962ba565f8ecee87db37e39b09e110bd6): same pools, recipe (lr 1e-4,
cosine, warmup 0.03, grad_accum 16, LoRA r 16 alpha 32 dropout 0.05 on the language model's
q/k/v/o/gate/up/down projections, vision tower and projector/connector frozen, NF4 double-quantised
base with bf16 compute, paged 8-bit AdamW, seed 42, nf4 evaluation, greedy decoding, 128 new tokens),
4-epoch schedule over the 1,120-item pools (70 optimizer steps per epoch, 280 in all), the same
280-item Q1_side dev set, the same STOPPING RULE (k* = smallest k in {1,2,3,4} with parse rate >= 0.90
AND >= 5 distinct parsed answers in EACH family for the metre-only adapter; otherwise k* = 4 and
"degenerate at the 4-epoch cap"), the mixed-unit adapter at the same k*, the same test cells and arms
(explicit m/cm/px, first-frame x4 on the metre arm, in-template m/cm, both test clips) and the same
392-item text probe, R1, R3, R4 exactly as round 1 and R2 as amended in round 2 (a cell counts toward
"replicates" only if R >= 10 AND Spearman rho(centimetre answers, reference) >= 0.30), the same
degeneracy readings and the same interpretation clause. Each backbone is judged on its own; a backbone
degenerate at the cap supports only a scale-boundary statement for that backbone.

DIFFERENCES from round 2, fixed now:
(a) No earlier base results exist for these models, so the bare backbone is run fresh on the same base
    cells (explicit arms, both test clips) and the same 392-item text probe; R3 uses them.
(b) Image policy, pinned per family, identical in training and evaluation, recorded in every receipt:
    Pixtral: longest edge capped at 512 px (image processor size.longest_edge = 512), i.e. 512x288 for
      a 960x540 frame: 576 patches of 16 px + 18 row-break tokens per frame, ~2.4k visual tokens per
      4-frame item, 147k px per frame (73% of Qwen's 200,704-px cap). Justification: the pixel-equal cap
      (592 px) would give ~800 tokens per frame, three times the visual tokens of every other family
      (256 per frame for Qwen, InternVL and Gemma3); 512 is the largest 16-px-aligned cap that keeps an
      item within ~2.5k visual tokens. The processor's own default (1024 px) is not used.
    Idefics3: the frozen SmolVLM2 family policy of the second-backbone runs (no image splitting,
      size.longest_edge = 384), which Idefics3-8B's 364-px vision encoder turns into one 364x364 view
      per frame (169 tokens per frame after pixel shuffle). Same policy object as SmolVLM2-2.2B.
    Gemma3: the processor's fixed 896x896 input per frame (256 tokens), pan-and-scan explicitly OFF.
    None matches Qwen's aspect-preserving pixel cap; reported, not tuned.
(c) Training reuses train/train_qlora.py and train/train_qlora_epochs.py byte-unchanged. Pixtral and
    Gemma3 are injected from outside by train/train_qlora_family.py (spec and policy from
    a100/family_policy.py). Idefics3 is already the frozen SmolVLM2 family; train/train_qlora_idefics3.py
    only renames the Idefics3Connector class to the name the frozen trainer's existing dtype hook
    looks for, so that hook (connector output cast to the embedding dtype) applies unchanged.
    train/train_durable.py adds crash safety only: a resumable checkpoint every 10 optimizer steps (the
    epoch checkpoints at steps 70/140/210/280 are among them and are never deleted), fsync before a
    checkpoint is marked complete, validation of the newest checkpoint and quarantine of an unreadable
    one, and automatic resume from the newest complete checkpoint (Trainer resume_from_checkpoint:
    optimizer, scheduler, RNG state and data position restored, the same 280-step cosine schedule).
    Saving does not change the optimisation. Every resume is logged (durable_resume_log.jsonl in the
    adapter directory) and reported; a resumed run is treated as the same run.
(d) Evaluation is the same code path (a100/eval_controls.py, tools/run_unit_probe.py) entered through
    tools/family_launch.py, which pins the image policy of (b) (Idefics3 through the frozen SmolVLM2
    loader exactly as the SmolVLM2 cells), writes result files atomically and fsyncs each appended
    prediction; an interrupted cell resumes from its intact prefix.
(e) Runs before this record: none on CourtDyn inputs for these models (only processor/tokenizer files
    were loaded locally to check prompt construction, without weights). Before the protocol runs, the
    A100 setup will run one smoke test per backbone into scratch directories: a 2-step training run of
    the v3 pool (interrupted after step 1 and resumed, to exercise (c) on the target machine; discarded),
    greedy answers of the bare backbone to 4 dev-set items, and one text-probe item answered with the
    2-step scratch adapter. They are disclosed here, are used for no decision, and no dev statistic or
    test cell is computed from them.
(f) A zero-shot sweep of public backbones (a100/exp_backbones.py, design in a100/README.md, T36) runs on
    the same machine after the trained arms; gated models without access are left out of it and listed.
    No decision rule is recorded for it; it is reported descriptively, with degenerate cells (<= 2
    distinct answers) kept separate.
No test-cell result may change k*, the recipe or these rules.

supersedes.why: the earlier record named Gemma3-4B, InternVL3-8B and Gemma3-12B; the backbone list was changed by the authors (Gemma is gated and access is pending) before anything had run -- no download, training, smoke test or evaluation of any backbone-4 model had happened. The earlier record stays in git history.

note: Local record, not externally timestamped. Revisions resolved from the Hugging Face API on 2026-09-28 (the Gemma revision is public metadata; its files need approved access).
